decisions.reason: A niche reusable citrus crate launched only a year ago still has unresolved market uncertainty, and keeping a single mould-based SKU in a large catalogue costs little, so the option is worth holding.
The foldable large container has its own page, which signals commitment and fits a core growing segment, so it is kept as a promising option.
A stackable crate is a low-cost extension of the firm's core range with little evidence of failure yet, so keeping it open is cheap.
A medium-duty rackable pallet fits established pallet demand and carries low holding costs while its prospects resolve.
The spill-retention pallet serves regulated safety demand and has a dedicated page, so its value looks likely enough to keep investing.
The pallet with load retainers is featured on its own page and is a cheap variant within the firm's pallet portfolio, so it is worth keeping while evidence accumulates.
